facts.fact: 她一路往东走（到 A 大道 D 街附近）越走越毛：身后无人——无流浪汉篝火、无老鼠、无警车；全是空地与黑灯楼——「街道是一张正在掉牙的嘴」。
facts.anchor: The street was a mouth with teeth falling out.

facts.fact: 爬楼（有一级台阶曾被她踩穿）时听不到音乐与人声，她有个可怕念头：整个街区会不会都消失了，她是最后一个，电影正要切黑。
facts.anchor: What if the whole neighborhood had disappeared, and I was the last one, and the movie was about to cut to black?

facts.fact: 楼上是空场：只有氛围道具（扫帚、脏床垫、唱机放着 Lotte Lenya 卷舌的《Mack the Knife》——母亲有这张、能用带意第绪腔的德语跟着唱）；Kurt 把驱逐通知糊满墙，空隙处贴上自己咧嘴笑的油印脸。
facts.anchor: Kurt had wheatpasted his eviction notices to the wall, covering everything, with assorted spaces filled in with mimeographed copies of his grinning face.

facts.fact: 众人在窗边抽烟；Kurt 盘腿坐在一圈祈愿蜡烛中——「定时到午夜烧尽」，Julie 说着翻了个白眼；她给他竖拇指，他点头。
facts.anchor: “They’re timed to burn down at midnight,” Julie said. Her back was to Kurt, and she rolled her eyes. I gave him a thumbs-up, and he nodded.

facts.fact: 她的低成本装扮：皱黑西装、尖领白衬衫、松开的红领带、裤腰插玩具手枪——「我是《漫长的告别》里的 Elliot Gould」；从 Julie 兜里拿烟叼在嘴上。（Cris 提醒缺一只猫，她掏出豆袋猫放肩上。）
facts.anchor: “I’m Elliot Gould in The Long Goodbye.” I took a cigarette from Julie’s pocket and let it dangle from my mouth.

facts.fact: Tanya 穿白褶裙黑腰带从舞池那头冲来：「这是个噩梦」——指着领带男（上东区）、骂另一个「Eurovulture」——「结束了！」
facts.anchor: “It’s a nightmare,” Tanya said. “Look at him,” she said as she pointed at a guy in a tie. “Upper East Side! And him,” she hissed. “Eurovulture! It’s over!”

facts.fact: Tanya 哭诉：派对往年都是我俩合办，他这次没问她；她本想做《灰色花园》主题——楼都要塌了；还有人送花（一束错位的兰花与玫瑰）。
facts.anchor: We always do this party together, and he didn’t even ask me. He said people were coming. I thought we could do Grey Gardens, you know, because the building’s falling apart?”

facts.fact: 她的诊断：Tanya 只是不想让 Kurt 抛下她往前走。Tanya 擦泪道谢（眼下留个黑渍）。
facts.anchor: “She just doesn’t want him to move on without her,” I said.

facts.fact: Julie 说了句「一切都烂透了」——「那男人还会连任」；一个衬衫男从她们中间挤过，像她们不存在。
facts.anchor: “God, everything is shit, isn’t it,” Julie said. “You know what else? That man is going to get reelected.” A guy in a button-down shirt pushed past us like we weren’t even there.

facts.fact: 她愣了一秒才反应过来她说的是总统大选——在这满城死亡的当中，大选有什么要紧？
facts.anchor: It took me a second to realize who she meant. What did a presidential election matter in the middle of all this death?

facts.fact: 停电之后她反而开了灯——「我的大脑，我意识到，太好了」：她知道该做什么、也知道怎么说服所有人跟她走。
facts.anchor: But now the lights were on in my head. My brain, I realized, was so good.

facts.fact: 行动号召：不能等，必须现在关停他们；Cris 摸不着头脑；她和 Julie 句句用斜体说话（可卡因加持）；Darryl 提醒停电了。
facts.anchor: “Right, because we have to shut them down.” Julie and I were both speaking in italics now.

facts.fact: 她描述那种派对情绪：夜到高点、人人疲惫又渴望狂欢、狂欢必须过量甚至带点暴力，因为缺的不只是玫瑰还有面包——那种势头若能装瓶，人头就要落地。
facts.anchor: There is a mood that settles over a party when the night has reached a certain high but everyone’s days have been particularly low and everyone’s fed up but also everyone wants a good time but that good time has to be excessive and maybe a little violent because everyone’s been a little deprived of not only roses but bread, too, and if you can bottle that mood, that momentum, heads will roll.

facts.fact: 「走」——他们在烹饪（暗语），被祝福；Joe 带起运动式口号「MU-cous MEM-brane」，众人下楼、Bianca 半路加入。
facts.anchor: “Okay, let’s move,” I said. We were cooking. We were blessed.

facts.fact: 上街时，像魔法一样，一辆横穿城区的巴士正停在 Kurt 公寓门前。
facts.anchor: And when we hit the street, there, like magic, was the crosstown bus, pulling up in front of Kurt’s apartment.
